content.title: Where to watch Illinois vs. UConn Final Four matchup for free tonight
content.text: Illinois guard Kylan Boswell (4) looks to pass around UConn guard Solo Ball during the first half of an NCAA college basketball game, Friday, Nov. 28, 2025, in New York. (AP Photo/Adam Hunger)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Jenna Malinowski | JMalinowski@mlive.comThe Illinois Fighting Illini and the UConn Huskies will square off in the Final Four this Saturday night, with a national championship berth on the line. What channel is UConn vs. Illinois on?Both Final Four matchups will be broadcast on TBS and TruTV. Illinois vs. UConn will start at 6:09 p.m. ET and Michigan vs. Arizona will start at 8:49 p.m. ET. Who are the announcers for the Final Four?Ian Eagle, Bill Raftery, Grant Hill and Tracy Wolfson will make up the broadcasting team for the Final Four.Final Four Streaming OptionsDirecTV Stream: DirecTV Stream’s Choice plan offers customers over 125 channels, including both TBS and TruTV. New subscribers can start with a five-day free trial and take $35 off their first month. Sling: Three different monthly plans are available to watch TBS on Sling. The streaming service also offers one, three and seven-day passes for customers looking to test it out or watch a specific game.HBO Max: In addition to hundreds of hit TV shows and movies, HBO Max’s standard plan offers fans access to live sports. This includes March Madness games, NHL on TNT and MLB on TBS. How does Sling’s day pass work?Sling’s one-, three- and seven-day passes are one-time subscriptions that allow customers access to the streaming service for the allotted amount of time. One-day passes start at $4.99, three-day passes start at $9.99 and seven-day passes start at $14.99.
